newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money steady, trading quiet.
newsitem.headline: German call money steady, trading quiet.

text.p: German call money was trading steady at about 3.00/05 percent on Tuesday, with little change expected in trading levels in coming days.

Traders expected an unchanged or slightly higher allocation from the Bundesbank in this week's regular repo. The Bundesbank might more than offset the expiring 67.5 billion marks to help banks' increased their reserve holdings, one said.

Banks' held 39.3 billion marks of reserves on Monday, for an average of 37.9 billion marks for the first 14 days of the month. Dealers said this was likely to be below the reserve requirement. Lombard borrowing totalled 100 million on Monday.
